role: pointwise existence via integer-programming flatness (Khinchine) on a convex relaxation of a slice
missing_theorem: One would need, for every prime p, a convex body K_p ⊂ ℝ^k whose lattice points are all ES certificates and whose lattice width exceeds the flatness constant Flt(k). This is impossible: by Steinhagen, width w forces an inscribed ball of radius ≫ w/√k, hence (for w ≫ k) a full unit lattice cube {a, a+1}^k ⊂ K_p; every ES slice is cut out by a nonzero polynomial of degree ≤ d in each variable (d = 1 for tuv − u − v = p and for the Type II divisor forms), which cannot vanish on a (d+1)^k grid. So any K_p of width ≫ dk contains non-certificates, and flatness can never force a certificate.
